# Keep a source useful after compression

Original text walkthrough. Read one segment at a time and stop at each pause. The text below is the complete transcript and can be used as captions for your own recording. There is no required audio or video. A 5–10 minute reading-and-pause session is a provisional estimate, not a measured runtime.

## Segment 1 · Start with the question

A traveler wants a print guide from a library on Friday. One Monday catalog observation concerns North branch print stock; a Tuesday record concerns South ebooks. Their dates are not the only difference.

**Pause before continuing:** List the fields needed to decide which observation applies.

## Segment 2 · Keep applicability attached

Compressing both records into “guide available” erases branch, format, and time. A useful compact packet keeps the fields that can change the decision, with source IDs.

**Pause before continuing:** Write a two-sentence packet without making a Friday availability promise.

## Segment 3 · Measure the loss

Ask the same questions of the long and short packets: which branch, which format, observed when, what remains unknown? A shorter packet that loses a decisive exception has not preserved the job.

**Pause before continuing:** Identify one detail you can remove and one that must remain; explain each.

## Segment 4 · Resume from evidence

A future session should find the source and know the next check. A memory note cannot make a past catalog snapshot current.

**Pause before continuing:** Write one executable next action and one invalidation condition.
